[[Statistics of the COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia#Cases by province and region|see cases by province]] }} [[File:Pelaksanaan Tes Swab di Badan Keuangan Daerah Sumbar.jpg|thumb|Health workers collect mucosal swab sample a COVID-19 test in [[Padang]], [[West Sumatra]].|220px]] The '''COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia''' is part of the [[COVID-19 pandemic|worldwide pandemic]] of [[COVID-19|coronavirus disease 2019]] (COVID-19) caused by [[severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2]] (SARS-CoV-2). It was confirmed to have spread to [[Indonesia]] on 2 March 2020, after a dance instructor and her mother tested positive for the virus. Both were infected from a Japanese national.{{cite web|title=First coronavirus cases confirmed in Indonesia amid fears nation is ill-prepared for an outbreak|url=http://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/02/first-coronavirus-cases-confirmed-in-indonesia-amid-fears-nation-is-ill-prepared-for-outbreak|date=2 March 2020|author=Rebecca Ratcliffe|work=The Guardian|access-date=2 March 2020}}{{cite news|agency=Reuters|title=Indonesia confirms first cases of coronavirus|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/1869789/indonesia-confirms-first-cases-of-coronavirus|work=Bangkok Post|access-date=2 March 2020|date=2 March 2020}} By 9 April 2020, the pandemic had spread to all [[Provinces of Indonesia|34 provinces]] in the country at that time. [[Jakarta]], [[West Java]], and [[Central Java]] are the worst-hit provinces, together accounting more than half of the national total cases. On 13 July 2020, the recoveries exceeded active cases for the first time.{{cite web|title=Indonesia's COVID-19 recoveries beat active cases for the first time|url=https://jakartaglobe.id/news/indonesias-covid19-recoveries-beat-active-cases-for-first-time|work=Jakarta Globe|access-date=25 July 2020|date=13 July 2020}} The number of deaths may be much higher than what has been reported as those who died with acute [[Symptoms of COVID-19|COVID-19 symptoms]] but had not been confirmed or tested were not counted in the official death figure.{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-indonesia-casualti/exclusive-more-than-2200-indonesians-have-died-with-coronavirus-symptoms-data-shows-idUSKCN22A04N|title=Exclusive: Flights from countries with high infection rate, including South Korea and Thailand, also continued to operate. Health experts and researchers at [[Harvard University]] in the United States expressed their concerns, saying that Indonesia is ill-prepared for an outbreak and there could be undetected COVID-19 cases.{{cite web |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/reported-cases-coronavirus-indonesia-200218112232304.html |title=Why Are There No Reported Cases of Coronavirus in Indonesia? |author1=Randy Mulyanto|author2=[[Febriana Firdaus]] |publisher=Al Jazeera |date=18 February 2020 |access-date=26 April 2020 }} On 2 March 2020, Indonesian president [[Joko Widodo]] announced the first cases in the country: a dance instructor and her mother in [[Depok]], [[West Java]].{{cite web|title=Presiden: Ibu-anak warga Indonesia positif COVID-19|url=https://www.antaranews.com/berita/1329602/presiden-ibu-anak-warga-indonesia-positif-covid-19|agency=Antara News Agency|access-date=7 April 2020|date=2 March 2020|author=Desca Lidya Natalia|editor=Zita Meirina|language=id}} Both of them had held a dance class at a restaurant in [[Kemang, Jakarta|Kemang]], [[South Jakarta]] on 14 February, which was attended by more than a dozen people. Corona|author=Isal Mawardi |website=Detik.com|language=id-ID|access-date=16 March 2020|date=16 March 2020}} == Classifications == === Cases === Since 14 July 2020, the [[Ministry of Health (Indonesia)|Ministry of Health of the Republic of Indonesia]] classifies people involved with COVID-19 into four levels:{{Cite news|url=http://sehatnegeriku.kemkes.go.id/baca/rilis-media/20200714/2834469/kemenkes-kenalkan-istilah-probable-suspect-kontak-erat-dan-terkonfirmasi-covid-19/|title=Kemenkes Kenalkan Istilah Probable, Suspect, Kontak Erat dan Terkonfirmasi COVID-19|date=14 July 2020|newspaper=Sehat Negeriku|access-date=15 July 2020}} * A '''suspect''' is a person showing symptoms of respiratory infections, and has stayed within 14 days in any country or any region in Indonesia with local transmission and/or has established contact within 14 days with a confirmed or probable case and/or requires treatment at the hospital and has no possible diagnosis of other diseases. * A '''probable case''' is a person, alive or deceased, who shows or showed obvious signs of COVID-19 symptoms and awaiting results of his or her swab test. * A '''confirmed case''' is a person whose sample produced positive results based on swab or molecular rapid test. A confirmed case may be symptomatic or asymptomatic. Due to lower accuracy and higher chance of false positives, a positive rapid or antibody test is not counted into the official number of cases. * A '''close contact''' is a person who established contact with a probable or confirmed case between 2 days before and 14 days after symptoms show up, or the date of testing for asymptomatic cases. The close contact must quarantine for 14 days. Reclassification into ''suspect'' may be done should if the person show symptoms. Other classifications include: * A '''recovered case''' is recorded after a confirmed case is discharged from isolation. For an asymptomatic case, it is 10 days after a sample testing; for a symptomatic case, it is after a swab test or 10 days after onset of symptoms, and at least 3 days after no fever or respiratory difficulties. * '''Death''' is recorded after someone who had been confirmed COVID-19 positive died. People who were classified into probable case's deaths are not counted in the official tally. === Location === According to the Ministry of Domestic Affairs, a regency or municipality may be classified into three levels depending on the severity of COVID-19 cases within the region, according to these parameters:{{cite news|title=Arti Zona Hijau, Kuning, dan Merah Daerah Corona versi Mendagri |date=30 May 2020 |url=https://kumparan.com/kumparannews/arti-zona-hijau-kuning-dan-merah-daerah-corona-versi-mendagri-1tW5rG3kNAY/full |work=KumparanNews |access-date=6 July 2020}} * The number of positive cases within 14 days * The number of suspected cases within 14 days * The number of deaths buried according to COVID-19 protocol within 14 days * Threat of disease contagions to healthcare workers Each has a score of 15 points for increasing trends, 20 for stationary trends, and 25 for decreasing trends. The three levels were assigned to a specific region: * '''Red Zone''' if the total score reaches below 80 points. Large-scale social restrictions may be enforced. * '''Yellow Zone''' if the total score reaches 80 to 95 points. * '''Green Zone''' if the total score reaches 100 points (all 4 parameters show a decreasing trend). == Cases == === Confirmed cases === {{Main|Statistics of the COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia#Cases by province and region}} [[Jakarta]] became the first province that confirmed COVID-19 cases, while [[Gorontalo]] was the last to do so. On 6 July 2020, [[Jambi]] became the last province to report a death, 53 days after the penultimate province [[East Nusa Tenggara]] did. [[West Java]] and [[Banten]] had ever reported 16,251 cases and 22,667 recoveries in a day respectively; both are the highest by a single province. [[Central Java]] hold the record for death numbers with 679. All six provinces in [[Java]] have the highest number of cases compared to other provinces, making it the worst-affected [[Regions of Indonesia|region]] in the country. === Suspected cases === Several Jokowi on 10 March 2020, urging countries with large populations, like Indonesia, to focus on increasing capacity of laboratoriums to detect cases of infection. [[Merdeka Palace|presidential palace]]. ==== Stimulus policy ==== ===== Phase 1 ===== To reduce the impact of COVID-19 pandemic to the national economy, on 25 February, the government released an IDR 10.3 trillion stimulus policy to the tourism sector, in the form of ticket price discounts and restaurant tax deductions. The IDR 10.3 trillion budget is given to provide discounted airplane ticket prices for 10 tourist destinations, such as [[Batam]], [[Denpasar]], [[Yogyakarta]], [[Labuan Bajo]], [[Lombok]], [[Malang]], [[Manado]], [[Lake Toba]] ([[Silangit Airport]]), [[Tanjung Pandan]], and [[Tanjungpinang]], which applies from March to May 2020. Ticket prices for low-cost airlines are discounted by 50%, medium-service by 48%, and full-service by 45%.{{Cite web|url=http://industri.kontan.co.id/news/pemerintah-tetapkan-insentif-penerbangan-tiket-pesawat-diskon-hingga-50|title=Pemerintah tetapkan insentif penerbangan, tiket pesawat diskon hingga 50%|date=25 February 2020|website=Kontan.co.id|language=id|access-date=15 March 2020}} Specifically for this ticket price discount, the stimulus fund comes from the IDR 444.39 billion state budget (APBN) for a discounted value of 30% and 25% of passengers per flight.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnnindonesia.com/ekonomi/20200226091352-532-478192/jurus-jokowi-lawan-virus-corona-dengan-diskon-tiket-pesawat|title=Jurus Jokowi Lawan Virus Corona dengan Diskon Tiket Pesawat|author=Aria Ananda|website=CNNIndonesia.com|language=id-ID|access-date=15 March 2020}} Additionally, there were additional IDR 100 billion ticket discounts paid by Angkasa Pura I and Angkasa Pura II and IDR 260 billion PT Pertamina paid through jet fuel price discounts, so the total ticket price stimulus was IDR 960 billion, so that the ticket price could be discounted by 50%.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wartaekonomi.co.id/read273843/lihat-nih-terbang-ke-10-destinasi-wisata-ini-diskonnya-hingga-50|title=Lihat Nih! Terbang ke 10 Destinasi Wisata Ini, Diskonnya hingga 50%|date=26 February 2020|website=Warta Ekonomi|language=id|access-date=15 March 2020}} The stimulus in the form of restaurant taxes borne by the central government was also provided amounting IDR 3.3 trillion. Thus, there was no restaurant tax in the ten tourist destinations above, but as compensation, the local government were to be given a grant from the central government. ===== Phase 2 ===== On 14 March. the government released an IDR 22.9 trillion stimulus policy. Among other policies, the government will bear 100% of the income tax of workers in the manufacturing sector with income up to IDR 17 million/month. This tax will be borne by the government or 6 months, from April to September, so the government will spend IDR 8,6 trillion.{{Cite web |last=Media |first=Kompas Cyber |date=2020-03-14 |title=Ini Daftar Stimulus Ekonomi untuk Redam Dampak Corona |url=https://money.kompas.com/read/2020/03/14/094137626/ini-daftar-stimulus-ekonomi-untuk-redam-dampak-corona |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=KOMPAS.com |language=id}} Besides fiscal stimus, the government also provided nonfiscal stimulus such as simplification of health certificates and V-legals, and reduction of export restrictions and prohibitions of 749 HS codes (443 fishery commodity HS codes and 306 logging industry HS codes). Simplifications as well as reduction of restrictions and prohibitions of raw material imports were also given to producers of steel, alloys, industrial salt, and powdered sugar. 735 export-import companies deemed reputable were given export-import process accelerations through automatic response and approval as well as write-off of surveyor reports. There were also general improvement and acceleration of export-import process service and supervision through the national logistics system. ===== Phase 3 ===== On 20 March 2020, the government is effectively able to use realocated state budget funds amounting to IDR 118.3-121.3 trillion to address the pandemic. The funds were realocated from funds for agency and ministry official travels, nonoperational expenses, and honorary employees amounting to IDR 62.3 trillion and village as well as regional transfers amounting to IDR 56-59 trillion.{{Cite web |last=JUD/DIM/LAS |date=2020-03-20 |title=Rp 121,3 Triliun untuk Tangani Covid-19 |url=https://www.kompas.id/baca/ekonomi/2020/03/21/rp-1213-triliun-untuk-tangani-covid-19 |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=kompas.id |language=id}} IDR 38 trillion of the realocated funds will be used for education, social safety net, and healthcare. IDR 6.1 trillion will be used for insurance of healthcare workers. BNPB will get an additional budget of IDR 3.3 trillion to address the pandemic. Some of the allocated village funds, amounting to IDR 72 trillion, will also be allocated to especially impacted villages.{{Cite web |last1=Wildan |first1=Muhammad |last2=Rahardyan |first2=Aziz |date=2020-03-21 |title=PENANGANAN WABAH COVID-19 : Eksekusi Anggaran Mendesak |trans-title=TACKLING THE COVID-19 PLAGUE : Budget Execution Is Urgent |url=https://koran.bisnis.com/read/20200321/244/1216241/surabaya.bisnis.com |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=Bisnis Indonesia |language=id}} ==== Medical devices incentives ==== On 20 March 2020, the [[Directorate General of Customs and Excise]] centralized permits of imports of medical devices for handling the pandemic to BNPB. Ministries/agencies, nonprofits, noncommercial private initiatives, and individuals can obtain medical device import tax allowance with a recommendation from BNPB. However, this tax allowance does not apply to commercial private initiatives and individuals and still requires permit from BNPB.{{Cite web |last=Tri |first=Rahma |date=2020-03-23 |title=Izin Impor Alkes Corona Dialihkan ke BNPB, Begini Prosedurnya |url=https://bisnis.tempo.co/read/1322897/izin-impor-alkes-corona-dialihkan-ke-bnpb-begini-prosedurnya |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=Tempo |language=en}} Fiscal incentives for medical device imports including import duty exemptions, value-added tax exemptions, and write-off of import trading administrations which would have to go through the [[Ministry of Trade (Indonesia)|Ministry of Trade]], [[BPOM]], and the [[Ministry of Health (Indonesia)|Ministry of Health]]. Medical devices included in this policy includes drugs, PPEs, face masks, and rapid test kits.{{Cite web |last=Kusuma |first=Hendra |title=Sri Mulyani Bebaskan Pajak Impor Alat Kesehatan Penanganan Corona |url=https://finance.detik.com/berita-ekonomi-bisnis/d-4949789/sri-mulyani-bebaskan-pajak-impor-alat-kesehatan-penanganan-corona |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=detikfinance |language=id-ID}} ==== Economic recovery policies ==== To recover from the economic impacts of the pandemic, the government planned to budget IDR 677 trillion for recovery policies.{{Cite web |last=Ramadhani |first=Pipit Ika |date=2020-06-03 |editor-last=Gideon |editor-first=Arthur |title=Anggaran Pemulihan Ekonomi Nasional Capai Rp 677 Triliun, Ini Rinciannya |trans-title=National Economic Recovery Budget Reaches IDR 677 Trillion, These Are The Details |url=https://www.liputan6.com/bisnis/read/4269634/anggaran-pemulihan-ekonomi-nasional-capai-rp-677-triliun-ini-rinciannya |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=Liputan 6 |language=id}} Economic growth for the period was projected to be similar to during the [[1997 Asian financial crisis|1997 crisis]].{{Cite web |last=Akhlas |first=Adran Wail |date=2020-06-04 |title=Indonesia unveils bigger stimulus worth $47.6 billion to fight coronavirus impacts - Business |url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/06/04/indonesia-unveils-bigger-stimulus-worth-47-6-billion-to-fight-coronavirus-impacts.html |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=The Jakarta Post}} Because the revised 2020 state budget was projected to grow by IDR 124.5 trillion, the 2020 state budget deficit reached IDR 1039.2 trillion or up to 6.34% of GDP{{Cite web |last=Bayu |first=Dimas Jarot |date=2020-06-03 |editor-last=Agustiyanti |title=Stimulus Ekonomi Bertambah, Defisit APBN Membengkak Jadi Rp 1.039,2 T - Before that, as explained by [[Ministry of Finance (Indonesia)|Minister of Finance]] [[Sri Mulyani]], the state budget deficit was IDR 859.2 trillion or 5.07% of GDP.{{Cite web |last=Kusuma |first=Hendra |title=Sri Mulyani Jelaskan Defisit APBN Melebar ke Rp 1.039 T |url=https://finance.detik.com/berita-ekonomi-bisnis/d-5043070/sri-mulyani-jelaskan-defisit-apbn-melebar-ke-rp-1-039-t |access-date=2024-05-03 |website=detikfinance |language=id-ID}} Consequently, the debt financing to cover the deficit increased from IDR 1006.4 trillion to IDR 1220.3 trillion, an increase of IDR 213.9 trillion. The charity was later reported to the police by [[Kotagede]] residents because the number of people collecting at these sites was in violation of the COVID restriction on gatherings. == Travel restrictions == Indonesia had denied transit and entry for all foreign visitors since 2 April 2020.{{Cite news|url=https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2020/03/31/20472021/imigrasi-larang-wna-masuk-ke-indonesia-mulai-2-april|title=Imigrasi Larang WNA Masuk ke Indonesia Mulai 2 April|author=Ardito Ramadhan|editor=Icha Rastika|website=Kompas.com|date=31 March 2020|language=id|access-date=31 March 2020}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/03/31/indonesia-to-bar-foreigners-from-entering-in-bid-to-curb-imported-cases.html|title=Indonesia to bar foreigners from entering in bid to curb imported cases|date=31 March 2020|author=Dian Septiari|work=The Jakarta Post|language=en|access-date=31 March 2020}} Indonesians who returned from China, South Korea, Italy, Iran, United Kingdom, Vatican City, France, Spain, Germany, and Switzerland were subject to additional health screening and a 14-day stay-at-home notice or quarantine depending on appearing symptoms.{{cite web |url=https://www.indonesia.travel/hk/en/news/advisory-on-coronavirus-for-travelers-to-indonesia |title=Advisory on Coronavirus For Travelers to Indonesia |work=Indonesia Travel |date=18 March 2020 |access-date=7 April 2020 }} [[Garuda Indonesia]], [[Citilink]], [[Lion Air]], [[Batik Air]], and [[Sriwijaya Air]] cancelled several flights and grounded their aircraft. Meanwhile, [[Indonesia AirAsia]] cancelled all flights. International airlines have either temporarily suspended services or continue operating with reduced frequency. Other airlines such as [[China Airlines]] and [[Etihad Airways]] chose to continue their services as usual.{{cite news|url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/travel/2020/03/28/airasia-indonesia-suspends-all-flights-starting-april-1.html|title=AirAsia Indonesia Suspends All Flights Starting 1 April|work=The Jakarta Post|date=28 March 2020|access-date=23 April 2020}}{{cite news|url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/03/09/more-than-12000-flights-canceled-in-two-months-over-virus-fears-says-angkasa-pura-i.html|title=More Than 12,000 Flights in Indonesia Have Been Cancelled|work=The Jakarta Post|date=9 March 2020|access-date=23 April 2020}} From 24 April until 8 June, the government suspended all passenger to travel outside areas with at least one confirmed case, regions that had imposed [[2020–21 Indonesia large-scale social restrictions|large-scale social restrictions]] (PSBB/LSSR), and those that had been declared COVID-19 red zones. The ban applied to all types of public and private transportation by [[Air travel|air]], [[Maritime transport|sea]], [[Land transport|land]], and railway, except for vehicles carrying leaders of state institutions, police and military vehicles, ambulances, fire trucks, hearses and vehicles transporting logistical supplies, staple goods and medicines. This suggests that Indonesia has a higher death rate than the official counts.{{cite news | agency = [[Reuters]] | date = 28 April 2020 | title = Indonesia's true coronavirus death toll could be over 2,000 higher, data shows | url = https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3081851/indonesias-true-coronavirus-death-toll-could-be-over-2000 | work = [[South China Morning Post]] | access-date = 28 April 2020 }} An analysis by ''[[Financial Times]]'' showed that there were 1,400 more deaths in Jakarta compared to the historical average number of deaths in March and April. This excess deaths figure is 15 times the official figure of 90 COVID-19 deaths in this same period.{{cite news |url=https://www.ft.com/content/6bd88b7d-3386-4543-b2e9-0d5c6fac846c |title=Global coronavirus death toll could be 60% higher than reported | author1=John Burn-Murdoch |author2=Valentina Romei |author3=Chris Giles |date= 26 April 2020|work=Financial Times }} === Travel restrictions and evasions === Prohibition of mudik for all of Indonesia was enacted after the pandemic worsens. In a 21 April teleconference, Jokowi announced that the government would prohibit mudik for residents of red zones. The prohibition was effective per 24 April. The implementation would be step-by-step; sanctions for violators was effective per 7 May.{{cite web |last=Idhom |first=Addi M |date=2020-04-21 |title=Larangan Mudik Berlaku Mulai 24 April 2020, Tapi Penerapan Bertahap |trans-title=Mudik Prohibition Effective Per 24 April, But Implementation Will Be Gradual |url=https://tirto.id/larangan-mudik-berlaku-mulai-24-april-2020-tapi-penerapan-bertahap-ePZX |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=tirto.id |language=id}} Previously, mudik prohibition was only effective for civil servants, [[BUMN]] employees, and [[Indonesian National Armed Forces|TNI]]-[[POLRI]].{{cite web |last=Mediatama |first=Grahanusa |date=2020-04-09 |editor-last=Laoli |editor-first=Noverius |title=Jokowi buka opsi larang mudik setelah mendapat banyak kritik |trans-title=Jokowi opens to possible mudik prohibition after receiving many critiques |url=https://nasional.kontan.co.id/news/jokowi-buka-opsi-larang-mudik-setelah-mendapat-banyak-kritik |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=kontan.co.id |language=id}} Initially, the government only advises people to not mudik. On 2 April, Presidential Speaker {{Interlanguage link|Fadjroel Rachman|id}} says that there was no official mudik prohibition for people with the caveat that pemudik must be supervised by local governments.{{cite web |last=Ihsanuddin |date=2020-04-02 |editor-last=Krisiandi |title=Pemerintah Tak Larang Mudik Lebaran, tetapi Ada Syaratnya |trans-title=The Government Doesn't Prohibit Mudik, But There is A Caveat |url=https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2020/04/02/12245691/pemerintah-tak-larang-mudik-lebaran-tetapi-ada-syaratnya |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426164103/https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2020/04/02/12245691/pemerintah-tak-larang-mudik-lebaran-tetapi-ada-syaratnya |archive-date=2020-04-26 |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=kompas.com |language=id}} The same was stated by ''ad interim'' [[Ministry of Transportation (Indonesia)|Minister of Transportation]] [[Luhut Pandjaitan]].{{cite web |date=2020-04-02 |title=Luhut Sebut Mudik Diperbolehkan, tapi Imbau Masyarakat Tak Pulang Kampung |trans-title=Luhut Said Mudik Is Permitted, But Advises People Not To |url=https://news.detik.com/berita/d-4962349/luhut-sebut-mudik-diperbolehkan-tapi-imbau-masyarakat-tak-pulang-kampung |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=Detik |language=id}} President Jokowi received criticisms for mudik regulations vagueness and decision-making slowness. With this revocation, Indonesia will enter an endemic period.{{Cite web |title=Pemerintah Resmi Cabut Status Pandemi COVID-19|url=https://setkab.go.id/pemerintah-resmi-cabut-status-pandemi-covid-19/ |website=Sekretaris Kabinet Republik Indonesia |date=21 June 2023 |language=id}} On 5 August 2023, President [[Joko Widodo]] officially ended the handling of the COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia. Jokowi also disbanded the Committee for Handling COVID-19 and National Economic Recovery or KPC PEN.{{Cite web |title=Akhiri Penanganan Pandemi Covid-19 di RI, Jokowi Bubarkan KPC PEN|url=https://www.kompas.tv/nasional/432033/akhiri-penanganan-pandemi-covid-19-di-ri-jokowi-bubarkan-kpc-pen |website=Kompas TV |language=id}} == Referral and examiner laboratories == On 16 March, [[Ministry of Health (Indonesia)|Minister of Health]] [[Terawan Agus Putranto]] officially signed the Minister of Health Decree HK.01.07MENKES/187/2020 which designated 1 national COVID-19 referral laboratory and 12 COVID-19 examiner laboratories. The Ministry of Health Research and Development Agency Laboratory was designated as the referral laboratory and while the other 12 laboratories are designated according to their locations throughout Indonesia.{{cite web |author=Tim detikcom |date=2020-03-17 |title=Ditetapkan Menkes, Ini Daftar 12 Laboratorium Pemeriksa COVID-19 |trans-title=Set By The Health Minister, These Are The 12 COVID-19 COVID-19 referral laboratory, the Agency Laboratory had the authority to confirm samples of COVID-19 patients obtained from the 12 examiner laboratories, to be forwarded to the {{Interlanguage The COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia is part of the worldwide pandemic of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). It was confirmed to have spread to Indonesia on 2 March 2020, after a dance instructor and her mother tested positive for the virus. Both were infected from a Japanese national.
By 9 April 2020, the pandemic had spread to all 34 provinces in the country at that time. Jakarta, West Java, and Central Java are the worst-hit provinces, together accounting more than half of the national total cases. On 13 July 2020, the recoveries exceeded active cases for the first time.
The number of deaths may be much higher than what has been reported as those who died with acute COVID-19 symptoms but had not been confirmed or tested were not counted in the official death figure.
Instead of implementing a nationwide lockdown, the government applied "Large-Scale Social Restrictions" (Indonesian: Pembatasan Sosial Berskala Besar, abbreviated as PSBB), which was later modified into the "Community Activities Restrictions Enforcement" (Indonesian: Pemberlakuan Pembatasan Kegiatan Masyarakat, abbreviated as PPKM). On 30 December 2022, the restrictions were lifted for all regions in Indonesia since satisfied population immunity exceeded the expectation, although it did not lift the pandemic status.
On 13 January 2021, President Joko Widodo was vaccinated at the presidential palace, officially kicking off Indonesia's vaccination program. As of 5 February 2023 at 18:00 WIB (UTC+7), 204,266,655 people had received the first dose of the vaccine and 175,131,893 people had been fully vaccinated; 69,597,474 of them had been inoculated with the booster or the third dose.
The pandemic is estimated to have caused at least 1 million excess deaths in Indonesia.
